workflows_experiments.experiment: Disjoint DEV parameter selection and TEST evaluation for an explicit three-score competing-belief heuristic versus a three-state probabilistic recurrent filter across six fixed revision/recovery utility trade-offs.

scientific_readiness_exploratory_results.observation: Across six fixed TEST utility trade-offs, the matched probabilistic filter won four and the explicit competing-belief heuristic won two; all utility differences were small.
scientific_readiness_exploratory_results.interpretation: Reduction pressure only: this simple synthetic world provides no robust mechanism-specific advantage for explicit competing beliefs once a strong probabilistic state baseline has matched persistent state and hysteresis opportunity.

hypothesis_or_reduction_question: Does an explicit competing-belief heuristic retain a mechanism-specific non-monotonic revision advantage over a strong probabilistic recurrent filter when both receive the same observations, three-scalar persistent-state budget, two DEV-selected control parameters, and revision hysteresis opportunity?

synthetic_or_dev_inputs_used.source: deterministic synthetic three-state non-monotonic Markov sequences only

implementation_or_experiment_performed: Implemented a three-score decayed competing-belief heuristic and a three-state HMM-style recurrent filter. Each independently DEV-selected two control parameters from fixed grids, then evaluated fixed selections on disjoint TEST seeds across six fixed accuracy/false-revision/switch-latency/return-recovery utility surfaces.
observations: The probabilistic filter won four of six TEST utility rows and the explicit competing-belief heuristic won two; maximum absolute utility gap was 0.0025821264 and mean absolute gap 0.0007901099, indicating near-equivalence in this bounded toy world.
what_would_falsify_or_reduce_it: A fresh prospective H1 task family with matched information/reliability access, persistent state, training/tuning/calibration, hysteresis opportunity and compute/resources where explicit competing objects show a stable held-out Pareto or preregistered utility advantage over strong probabilistic/recurrent controls.
candidate_formal_question: Under prospectively matched observation access, persistent-state capacity, training/tuning/calibration budget, revision-control opportunity and compute/resource budget, do explicit persistent competing beliefs improve held-out non-monotonic revision accuracy/recovery/latency trade-offs beyond strong probabilistic or generic recurrent state models?
